notes: Port-kind fixes: the catalogue's Grove cable (grove-cable-4pin-f) has socket-kind ports, which cannot join the carrier's Grove header or the sensor's pins. It is replaced by a new type, grove-cable-4pin-grove, with the same 8 port names and through pairs (A1-B1 and so on) but pin-hole ports. Pin into pin-hole is a valid pair, and the carrier's A6 Grove connector and the sensor pins are pins.
The carrier's relay terminals are now header-socket kind, so the pump's lead and the USB cable's wire-end are valid joins into them. In reality they are screw terminals that clamp a wire.
The open-ended USB cable's usb-a plug is kind ball, which pairs with the adapter's socket-kind USB-A port (a plug-into-receptacle join). This is a stand-in, because no USB-specific kind exists.

The carrier has a single A6 port for the Grove connector, so the Grove cable's four conductors are shown as one connection from grove1 A1 to carrier A6. The sensor end is wired pin by pin (B1 SIG, B2 NC, B3 VCC, B4 GND).
The pump is wired as the tutorial says: open-ended cable positive to relay 1 NO, pump positive (port 1, the supply side) to relay 1 COM, and the cable negative joined to the pump negative (port 2).
The usb-power-adapter type has only one USB-A port (A), so both USB cables go to port A as a simplification. The tutorial says the adapter has at least 2 USB ports.
Relay 1 is the one used in the circuit text, although the code drives opla.Relay2. The circuit text and image take priority, so relay 1 is wired.
The watering pipe, water container and optional connector strip are left out because they are not electronic parts. No breadboard or jumper wires are used.
